note: P39 (a)/(c) in situ at the production cadence (d=128, B=8, K=64 — the exact 40h POS config), measured independently on two machines, 2026-07-25.

cadence_probe.note: snapshot size scales with MODEL, not with chunk weight — so raising chunk weight shrinks the snapshot cost measured in chunk slots (7.94 -> 2.59), which is the whole mechanism behind the (a) ratio

verdict: Two independent machines agree, and both refute the projection that stood in for this measurement. (a) 7.09x on the Mac, 5.60x on beast — better than the toy cadence 17.9x, still far above the 3.0 threshold. (c) 2.22x and 2.04x — better than toy 3.79x, still above 1.0. The shared-core hypothesis for (c) is REFUTED: beast gives B its own cores among 16 and the ratio barely moves (2.22 -> 2.04). The cpu numbers show why: B spends 45.4 s replaying what cost A 22.3 s to produce — almost exactly 2x. Catch-up replay is intrinsically about twice as expensive per chunk as live streaming, independent of machine and of core contention. (c) as registered (< 1.0) asks replay to be FASTER than production; nothing in these two runs suggests it can be. (b) state parity passes on both machines, exact heldout match — unchanged at every cadence and every machine tried.
